note: Ingredient rules for the Food Check Android app. AVOID requires demonstrated human harm at realistic eating amounts, NOT merely 'banned somewhere'. Every entry must state its harm dose in howMuch.

avoid.name: Partially hydrogenated oils (artificial trans fat)
avoid.why: The one additive proven to harm people at everyday amounts, it raises bad cholesterol, lowers good cholesterol, and increases heart-attack risk.
avoid.howMuch: About 4-5 g a day (two teaspoons) raises heart-disease risk by roughly a quarter. There's no amount that helps you, so zero is the target.
avoid.bannedIn: USA, EU, and most of the world

avoid.name: Potassium bromate
avoid.why: A bread-flour additive that causes cancer in animals by damaging DNA. Health experts refused to set any safe level for it.
avoid.howMuch: No safe level exists. Properly baked bread burns off most of it, but under-baked bread can keep some, and there's no reason to accept any.
avoid.bannedIn: EU, UK, Canada, China, India; California from 2027

avoid.name: Brominated vegetable oil (BVO)
avoid.why: Builds up in your fat and can harm the thyroid and nerves. It has been illegal in US food since August 2025, if you find it, the product is out of date.
avoid.howMuch: People who drank 2-4 litres of BVO citrus soda a day for weeks developed headaches, memory loss and trouble walking. It's now illegal at any level.

warning.name: Nitrites / nitrates (curing salts)
warning.why: In cured meat these turn into compounds tied to bowel cancer. Processed meat is the one food the World Health Organization calls a definite cause of cancer in people.
warning.howMuch: Every 50 g of processed meat a day (two slices of bacon or one hot dog) raises bowel-cancer risk by about 18%. Occasional is fine; daily is the problem.

warning.name: Red dye No. 3 (erythrosine)
warning.why: Being removed from US food by January 2027. It caused thyroid tumours in male rats through a hormone route that doesn't work the same way in people, the FDA itself says there's no evidence it causes cancer in humans.
warning.howMuch: The rat tumours needed the dye to be about 4% of everything the animal ate, for life, roughly 100,000 times more than anyone gets from food.

warning.name: Titanium dioxide
warning.why: A white colouring. Europe removed it in 2022 because it couldn't rule out DNA damage, but the USA, Canada, the UK, Australia and the World Health Organization all reviewed it and found no health concern.
warning.howMuch: No harmful amount has ever been found. Less than one part in a thousand is absorbed by the body; it mostly passes straight through.
warning.bannedIn: EU (2022), still allowed in the USA

warning.name: Propylparaben
warning.why: A preservative Europe removed from food over possible hormone effects in young rats. A later, larger study found nothing, and most of what people absorb comes from cosmetics rather than food.
warning.howMuch: The rat effect needed about 700 mg a day scaled to an adult. Food gives you well under 1 mg a day, about a thousand times less.

warning.name: BHA / BHT
warning.why: Preservatives that stop fats going rancid. BHA caused tumours in the forestomach of rats, an organ people don't have. The FDA reopened the safety review of both in 2026.
warning.howMuch: The rat tumours needed BHA to be 2% of everything the animal ate, about a thousand times what people get. The one real gap: children who eat a lot of packaged food can go over the BHT limit.

warning.name: Artificial food dyes (Red 40, Yellow 5, Yellow 6)
warning.why: Can worsen attention and hyperactivity in some children. In Europe these foods must carry a warning label. US makers have promised to remove them, but there's no law forcing it.
warning.howMuch: Behaviour changes showed up in children at 20-60 mg a day, one brightly coloured drink or a handful of sweets. No effect has been found in adults.

warning.name: Erythritol
warning.why: A sugar substitute in "keto" and sugar-free foods. Recent research found it makes blood platelets stickier, which could raise clot, stroke and heart-attack risk. Not proven yet, but worth knowing if your heart is a concern.
warning.howMuch: One serving (about 30 g, the amount in a single sugar-free drink or dessert) was enough to change platelet behaviour for hours in healthy volunteers.

warning.name: Aspartame
warning.why: The diet-drink sweetener. The World Health Organization's cancer agency calls it "possibly" cancer-causing, but the same organisation's safety panel kept the daily limit unchanged and found no reason to worry.
warning.howMuch: You'd have to drink about 14 cans of diet soda every day to reach the safe limit. The one real rule: anyone born with the condition PKU must avoid it completely.

warning.name: Cyclamate
warning.why: A sweetener banned in the USA in 1970 over a cancer scare that later fell apart, the FDA's own scientists cleared it in 1984. It stays on this list only because its safe daily limit is lower than other sweeteners.
warning.howMuch: About 5 cans a day of a cyclamate-sweetened drink reaches the safe limit, the tightest margin of any sweetener, so don't drink it all day.
